data.title: Keel Infrastructure (KEEL) Exits Bitcoin And Bets On AI Data Centers
data.description:
• Keel Infrastructure (NasdaqGM: KEEL) has sold its entire Bitcoin treasury and exited direct exposure to the cryptocurrency market.
  • The business is refocusing on building and leasing high-capacity data centers tailored to AI and high-performance computing workloads.
  • This change marks a material shift in Keel Infrastructure's long term plan away from cryptocurrency mining toward digital infrastructure services.

Keel Infrastructure runs digital and energy infrastructure that caters to high-performance computing and AI workloads across North America, which puts it squarely in the path of customers needing dense power, cooling, and reliable uptime for compute-heavy tasks. This positioning gives the business a clear operational link between this news and demand from AI and HPC clients.

1 thing going right for Keel Infrastructure that this headline doesn't cover.

How does selling the Bitcoin stack change Keel Infrastructure’s business model?

The shift takes Keel Infrastructure away from balance sheet exposure to Bitcoin prices and pushes it toward earning rent like income from AI and HPC tenants. Instead of holding 2,520 coins worth about US$192 million, the business is now leaning on its 2.2 GW development pipeline to drive future leasing. That moves risk from crypto volatility to construction, power and tenant demand.

Does this change the Keel Infrastructure Narrative?

The move lines up closely with the existing Narrative, which already framed Keel as an AI data center developer relying on long term leases and secured megawatts. Exiting Bitcoin holdings reinforces the catalyst around commercializing powered land at Panther Creek, Sharon and Moses Lake, while keeping the existing risks about funding costs and permitting delays firmly in play.

What should investors watch next to test whether this pivot is working?

The key proof point is signed, multi year leases on the new AI and HPC campuses, especially Moses Lake where construction has started and management has flagged 2027 as the first revenue year. Concrete metrics would be disclosed megawatts under contract, pricing per kilowatt and any update on cash runway as Q4 2026 and early 2027 results come through.

For you as an investor, that deal places more emphasis on Privia Health Group’s ability to integrate another ACO, maintain quality metrics and keep care margin healthy while still exiting less central arrangements like Montana. Missteps in onboarding those attributed lives or weaker performance in value based contracts would quickly test the current catalyst narrative.

Privia Health Group’s current analyst storyline points to US$3.1b in revenue and US$93.8 million in earnings by 2029, based on forecasts that assume 9.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$65.7 million from US$28.1 million today.

The Two Target Stories Investors Had To Balance

The shares cost US$91.94 at the start of the period. Anyone weighing Target then had to decide whether margin pressure or a cleaner, more efficient retailer would define the next few years.

The bullish narrative saw a fair value of US$103, a price implied by expectations that investments in technology, private labels, digital platforms, and supply chain agility would support better margins and market share.

data.title: What Hansen Technologies Bears Saw Before The Fall
data.description:
If analysts were still arguing in late 2025 about whether Hansen Technologies deserved a premium P/E for its billing software niche, the following year gave investors a much starker scorecard. Investors who held Hansen Technologies over the past year are down 37.3%, including dividends. If you were weighing a fresh position at the 2025 decision date, how much of that eventual drawdown was hinted at by the split bull and bear cases already on record?

Hansen Technologies has already moved. See which of 4 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Two Stories Investors Had To Weigh On Hansen Technologies

The shares cost A$5.93 at the start of the period, and investors in Hansen Technologies were choosing between two very different stories about what that price implied.

The bullish view saw a fair value of A$6.51. This represented a notional long term worth if digital modernization in utilities and telecom kept supporting recurring, high margin SaaS contracts and if AI driven automation improved efficiency.

The bearish camp anchored on a fair value of A$4.6. This assumed rising GDPR compliance costs and low cost SaaS rivals would keep pressuring profitability and retention.

What The Hansen Technologies Results Put To The Test

The clearest datapoint was the H2 2026 result. Total revenue slipped from A$214.156m in H2 2025 to A$195.178m, while net income moved from A$43.254m to A$25.721m. Net margin went from 20.2% to 13.2%. That combination challenged the bullish view that Hansen Technologies could rely on resilient, high-margin recurring SaaS earnings.

The main lesson is practical. When a case leans on durable profitability, watch net margin as closely as revenue. For another software stock with a “recurring and sticky” pitch, compare the claimed margin profile with what the income statement reports over time.

What Hansen Technologies Buyers Are Really Betting On Now

Hansen Technologies trades at A$3.61 today, with the selected Narrative setting its Fair Value above that level based on a different read of the future cash flows. The gap reflects a view that the current price underplays what a reshaped mix of contracts and regions might produce.

This Narrative leans on AI enabled cost savings, a heavier recurring and consumption based revenue mix, and EMEA growth offsetting German energy delays. A buyer at today’s price would need to believe Hansen Technologies can execute on AI driven product and go to market plans well enough to support higher long run margins.

"Ongoing AI enabled productivity programs, including tools embedded across development and corporate workflows and at least eight AI enabled products in market, are already linked to $20 million of operating cost removal and higher EBITDA margins in FY26 and are expected to keep supporting group net margins and earnings quality as Hansen Technologies extends this approach."
